title: Sun-like star caught after eating one of its own planets
hook: Stars aren't supposed to be rich in lithium — so when astronomers found a Sun-like star packed with it, the likely explanation was grim: it had just swallowed one of its own planets.
key_points: A distant Sun-like star shows an unusually high concentration of lithium in its atmosphere.
Stars normally burn through lithium over time, so a surplus signals swallowed planetary material.
Comparisons with dozens of similar stars confirmed the signal is genuinely unusual.
A massive brown dwarf companion may have nudged the planet into a fatal plunge.
content_html: According to a ScienceDaily report, astronomers say a distant Sun-like star appears to have devoured one of its own planets, leaving behind a surprising chemical fingerprint: an unusually high concentration of lithium. Because stars normally burn through their lithium over time, a surplus is a strong sign that planetary material was recently mixed into the star.
extra_html: Researchers made careful comparisons with dozens of similar stars to confirm the signal was genuinely unusual rather than ordinary variation. They think a massive brown dwarf companion may have gravitationally nudged the planet inward, sending it on a fatal plunge into its star.

related.title: What Powers the Sun
related.hook: The Sun isn't burning like a fire — it's fusing hydrogen into helium in its core, and a sliver of mass turning into pure energy is what lights up our sky.
